reality.qualifier: MotorTrend Road-Trip Range Test, constant 70 mph, all-terrain tires (per Tesla's spec for 318 mi rating), 95% battery utilization with safety buffer.
reality.verbatim_quote: In the MotorTrend Road-Trip Range Test, the 2024 Tesla Cybertruck Dual Motor Foundation Series covered 224 miles, or 94 miles less than its official 318-mile range… falling 30 percent short of the window-sticker number places the Cybertruck among the worst performers in our database of 56 EVs

sources.name: MotorTrend — 2024 Tesla Cybertruck Dual Motor Real-World Range Test
Recharged — Tesla Cybertruck Real World Highway Range

narrative_one_liner: Cybertruck Dual Motor advertised 318 mi; MotorTrend 70 mph test measured 224 mi — 30% gap, among worst in their 56-EV database.
narrative: Tesla advertises 318 mi range for the Cybertruck Dual Motor (Foundation Series with all-terrain tires). MotorTrend's instrumented 70 mph Road-Trip Range Test measured 224 mi — a 94-mile, 29.6% gap. MotorTrend characterized this as 'among the worst performers in our database of 56 EVs.' Recharged's synthesis of multiple independent tests puts typical highway range in the mid-200s. The Cybertruck's brick-shaped aerodynamics and weight make it especially prone to highway-speed range collapse.
methodology_notes: MotorTrend's Road-Trip Range Test uses 95% of battery capacity (deliberately leaves 5% safety buffer) at constant 70 mph. This is a stricter test than EPA combined-cycle but mirrors how owners actually use the vehicle on road trips.
caveats: The 224 mi result was from a Foundation Series early-production unit; later production may have software-driven efficiency improvements.
Aero wheel covers are a known efficiency factor; Tesla stopped delivering them after early customer reports of tire sidewall wear, but has not updated the range claim accordingly.
MotorTrend's 95%-utilization protocol is more conservative than running to dashboard zero; some owners report 240–270 mi if they push to true empty.
alternative_explanations: All-terrain tires are documented to cost ~22 mi vs all-season; the 318 mi rating is for the AT-tire config, so this is not the issue.
Cold weather exacerbates the gap; MotorTrend's test was in moderate conditions.
